Let <MATH_0001> be a ringed space. A first order thickening
<MATH_0002> is said
to be <TEXTITOPEN_0001>trivial<TEXTITCLOSE_0001> if there exists a morphism of ringed spaces
<MATH_0003> which is a
left inverse to <MATH_0004>. The choice of such a morphism
<MATH_0005> is called a <TEXTITOPEN_0002>trivialization<TEXTITCLOSE_0002> of the first order thickening.
Given <MATH_0006> we obtain a splitting
<MATH_0007>
as sheaves of algebras on <MATH_0008> by using <MATH_0009> to split the surjection
<MATH_0010>. Conversely, such a splitting determines
a morphism <MATH_0011>. The category of trivialized first order thickenings of
<MATH_0012> is equivalent to the category of 
<MATH_0013>-modules.
